cohort: The cohort consisted of 112 singleton pregnancies with bleeding after 28 weeks gestation, diagnosed with antepartum haemorrhage, enrolled at a tertiary care centre.
finding: Antepartum haemorrhage (APH) had an incidence of 1.15%, primarily caused by abruptio placentae (46.43%) and placenta previa (42.86%), with major placenta previa significantly increasing haemorrhage risk (OR 3.18).
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was required in 82.1% of placenta previa cases.
